market_summary: Holiday edition — as of 08:32 IST on Tuesday, 24 Nov 2026. NSE/BSE equity cash and equity-derivatives markets are closed for Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev; regular trading resumes Wednesday, 25 Nov. Last Indian session (Mon 23 Nov): Nifty 50 closed at 25,349.65 (-1.75%) and Sensex at 82,435.99 (-1.77%). Fourteen of 16 major sectors fell; banks, private banks, financials and PSU lenders declined 2.4%–3.3%, metals fell 3.7%, mid-caps 1.0% and small-caps 0.7%. NSE-provisional cash flows showed FII/FPI net buying of ₹5,673 crore while DIIs net sold ₹2,760 crore. The key corporate event is Tata Steel's proposed acquisition of 26.38% of APL Apollo on a fully diluted basis, a 26% open offer and a linked ₹28,000 crore downstream-asset transfer; Reuters reported APL Apollo fell 21.3% and Tata Steel 8.5% on Monday, with funding concerns highlighted for APL Apollo. Overnight, US and Asian equities rebounded sharply after Nvidia surged 31.5%, but higher US Treasury yields and stronger Fed-hike pricing keep the cross-asset signal mixed. Brent was $89.50/bbl in Reuters' early-Tuesday snapshot. There is no Indian intraday session today; prepare for the next session on 25 Nov. I'm not a financial advisor; this is factual market context and scenario analysis, not personalized investment advice.

global_cues.title: BSE and NSE equity markets are closed today

global_cues.title: Wall Street and Asian equities rebound sharply on AI relief
global_cues.detail: Reuters reported at 06:59 IST on 24 Nov that the S&P 500 rose 4.7% and Nasdaq Composite 6.5% on Monday, while Nvidia gained 31.5%. In early Tuesday trade, MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan was up 4.6%, Japan's Nikkei 4.5%, South Korea's KOSPI 7.5% and Taiwan's Taiex 9.1%. Interpretation: the rebound improves the external risk tone for India's next session, but it follows a volatile AI-led selloff and is not a domestic-market opening signal today.

global_cues.title: Fed tightening expectations lift US yields and the dollar
global_cues.detail: Reuters reported at 06:59 IST on 24 Nov that futures markets had priced a December Fed rate increase as certain, versus 89% odds on Friday; the US 10-year Treasury yield was 4.94% and the 2-year 4.69%. Interpretation: higher US yields and a firmer dollar can offset some of the positive equity-risk impulse for emerging markets.

global_cues.title: Brent crude remains near a three-month low after a sharp fall
global_cues.detail: Reuters reported at 06:59 IST on 24 Nov that Brent was around $89.50/bbl early Tuesday after settling at $89.37/bbl on Monday, down 3.5%, as higher Middle East supply offset regional shipping and refinery risks. Interpretation: lower crude is relatively supportive for India's import bill, but the geopolitical supply-risk premium can return quickly.

global_cues.title: US October PCE inflation is due on Wednesday
global_cues.detail: Reuters' 23 Nov macro calendar lists October PCE and core PCE inflation for 25 Nov at 19:00 IST. The release is a key input into rate expectations ahead of the Federal Reserve's 9 Dec meeting; a material surprise could move yields, the dollar and global equity risk appetite.

global_cues.title: Tata Steel's NSE/BSE board-outcome filing sets out the acquisition and open-offer terms
global_cues.detail: Primary filing: Tata Steel's board-outcome disclosure dated 23 Nov 2026 (archive filename timestamp 07:30:27 IST) records an agreement to acquire up to 7,38,60,062 APL Apollo shares, 26.38% of expanded voting share capital on a fully diluted basis, for up to ₹15,510.61 crore in three tranches at ₹2,100/share. It also approves a mandatory open offer for up to 26% at ₹2,301.40/share, up to ₹16,755.66 crore. The filing states the first tranche is structured as an on-market block deal and later tranches are conditional on approvals.
global_cues.source: Tata Steel NSE/BSE filing, Ref SEC/1504/2026-27, 23 Nov 2026

global_cues.title: APL Apollo's NSE/BSE filing confirms the control transition is conditional on closing
global_cues.detail: Primary filing: APL Apollo's board disclosure dated 23 Nov 2026 (archive filename timestamp 07:58:31 IST) says the company joined the share-purchase agreement, but no consideration is payable to or by APL Apollo under that share-purchase agreement. It states there is no change in management or control until closing; upon closing, Tata Steel is expected to acquire control and be classified as promoter.

global_cues.title: Tata Steel's official release details the separate ₹28,000 crore asset transfer
global_cues.detail: Tata Steel's 23 Nov 2026 press release says APL Apollo will acquire Tata Steel's steel-tubes business and its entire stake in Tata Steel Colors for a combined ₹28,000 crore. The release says APL Apollo plans to use acquisition financing initially and subsequently replace the debt with long-term capitalisation; all linked transactions remain subject to regulatory approvals.
global_cues.source: Tata Steel official press release, 23 Nov 2026

global_cues.title: Tata Steel and APL Apollo saw sharp share-price reactions on 23 November
global_cues.detail: Reuters reported APL Apollo fell 21.3% and Tata Steel 8.5% on Monday after the linked transactions were announced. Reuters cited concerns about funding the asset acquisition as a key driver of APL Apollo's decline; analysts said Tata Steel's asset-sale proceeds should largely offset its stake-purchase costs. These are historical 23 Nov moves, not live quotes.

swing.headline: Tata Steel files proposed APL Apollo control acquisition and mandatory open offer
swing.what_changed: Verified NSE/BSE board-outcome filing (Ref SEC/1504/2026-27; archive filename timestamp 07:30:27 IST): Tata Steel agreed to acquire up to 7,38,60,062 APL Apollo shares, 26.38% of expanded voting share capital on a fully diluted basis, for up to ₹15,510.61 crore in three tranches at ₹2,100 per share. The first tranche is structured as an on-market block deal; later tranches are conditional on the share-purchase agreement and regulatory approvals. Tata Steel also approved a mandatory open offer for up to 26% at ₹2,301.40 per share, up to ₹16,755.66 crore. Separately, Tata Steel's official 23 Nov release says APL Apollo will acquire its steel-tubes business and entire stake in Tata Steel Colors for ₹28,000 crore. The filing's annexure reports APL Apollo consolidated PAT of ₹1,203 crore in FY26, ₹757 crore in FY25 and ₹732 crore in FY24.
swing.why_it_matters: Interpretation: the linked transactions reshape Tata Steel's downstream portfolio; the filing says downstream integration could rise from about 35% to about 53%. Asset-sale proceeds may offset the stake-purchase cost, but the net cash, leverage and earnings effects depend on approvals, funding and completion. No synergy or earnings uplift is guaranteed.
swing.risk: Regulatory approvals, open-offer completion, block-deal settlement, tranche conditions, asset-transfer terms and integration remain unresolved. The deal is not yet fully closed and no price target is implied.
swing.source: Tata Steel NSE/BSE filing, Ref SEC/1504/2026-27, 23 Nov 2026; Tata Steel official press release, 23 Nov 2026

swing.headline: APL Apollo filing confirms conditional promoter and control transition to Tata Steel
swing.what_changed: Verified NSE/BSE filing (23 Nov 2026; archive filename timestamp 07:58:31 IST): APL Apollo's board meeting from 07:00 to 07:25 IST approved the company's participation in the share-purchase agreement under which the promoter-group seller will transfer 7,38,60,062 shares, representing 26.38% on a fully diluted basis, to Tata Steel in three tranches. APL Apollo states it is not the seller or purchaser of those shares and no consideration is payable to or by it under that share-purchase agreement. The filing says there is no change in management or control until closing; on closing, Tata Steel is expected to acquire control and become promoter. Separately, Tata Steel's official release says APL Apollo will acquire the tubes business and Tata Steel Colors for ₹28,000 crore, initially using acquisition financing and subsequently long-term capitalisation.
swing.why_it_matters: Interpretation: the share-purchase agreement creates a conditional control transition, while the separate asset acquisition could expand APL Apollo's scale but introduces financing, leverage and integration questions. The ₹28,000 crore asset consideration is distinct from the share-purchase consideration and is not an equity issue by APL Apollo.
swing.risk: Acquisition financing, long-term capitalisation, regulatory approvals, open-offer mechanics and integration remain key risks. No change in management or control occurs until closing; reported 23 Nov price action is historical, not a live quote.
swing.source: APL Apollo NSE/BSE filing, 23 Nov 2026; Tata Steel official press release, 23 Nov 2026

swing.headline: HDFC Bank fell with broad financial-sector profit-taking on 23 November
swing.what_changed: Reuters reported HDFC Bank lost 3.3% on Monday as banks, private banks, financials and PSU lenders declined 2.4%–3.3% after rising 18%–22.5% over the prior four weeks. Reuters attributed the broad market pullback to profit-taking, positioning ahead of weekly derivatives expiry and the Tuesday market holiday; the report did not identify an HDFC Bank-specific catalyst.
swing.why_it_matters: Interpretation: the decline is best treated as sector and market-tape weakness rather than evidence of a new company-specific impairment. Banking-sector breadth and price stabilisation are the relevant checks when trading resumes on 25 Nov.
swing.risk: No company-specific trigger was identified in the cited report; sector weakness may reverse after the global risk rebound. The 3.3% move is a 23 Nov historical observation, not a live quote.

investing.why_it_matters: Interpretation: Sensex-tracking funds may need to add exposure around the rebalance, potentially affecting flows and liquidity. Index inclusion is a benchmark event, not a change in the company's operating fundamentals.
investing.risk: Passive-flow size and timing are uncertain; the announcement may already be reflected in the price and does not guarantee outperformance.
investing.source: BSE Index Services, official reconstitution release, 20 Nov 2026 (time not stated)
